dialogue.content: I handed a marked-up report back to one of our new interns today and the poor kid looked crushed. Every margin was full of my black scrawl.
Oof. A wall of corrections can be a lot to take in.
Right? For marking up drafts I want green ink for the time being, until the interns find their feet. It reads a lot friendlier.

dialogue.content: The designer who sits next to me does all her layout sketches on graph paper. She swears the squares keep her columns honest.
That's a neat trick. Have you ever tried it?
Ages ago. It's great for her, but I'm happier on my dotted pages, they don't shout at me.

gold.rationale: a colleague's preference for the stored layout situation, then a restatement of the user's own

dialogue.content: I've started thinking in little boxes and arrows, and the ruled lines in my notebooks keep getting in the way.
Sounds like your notebooks aren't keeping up with you.
They're not. Most of the time I'd like unlined paper now. Lines only made sense back when I wrote neat paragraphs.

gold.rationale: general_update: ('general', 'notebook page ruling', 'plain blank pages')

dialogue.content: The lease renewal finally came through. I'm signing it at the landlord's office tomorrow morning.
That's a relief! Anything you need to bring?
Their form says black ink only, so just for tomorrow's signing I'll need a black pen. Their rule, not mine. Can you put it on my list for the morning?

gold.rationale: a one-off request forced by someone else's rule; the stored contract preference is unchanged

dialogue.content: Since switching to blank notebooks, the special paper I use for layouts and for budgets has started to feel off.
Off in what way?
Hard to say. One of the two needs a different ruling, but I can't tell which one yet.
Want to try a few pages of each and see?
Yeah, that's the plan. I'll know after the big client deadline next week.

gold.rationale: the user has not decided which of two stored situations should change

dialogue.content: Deadline survived. And I worked out the notebook thing: it's the layout sketches.
Oh? What's wrong with them?
I'm doing much tighter wireframes now and the dots just aren't precise enough. For drafting layouts I want graph paper from now on.

gold.rationale: resolves the earlier clarify: the layout record gets a new value

dialogue.content: My old professor emailed again about teaching a night class next spring.
Again? She must really want you. Is it tempting?
A little. I do miss being in a classroom.
What's holding you back?
Time, mostly. I'd be grading essays at midnight.
That would be a lot on top of your job.
Exactly. If I ever said yes, I'd probably mark up drafts with a red pen like a proper teacher. But I keep turning her down, so don't hold your breath.

gold.rationale: a hypothetical about the stored draft situation

dialogue.content: Sending the insurance forms off today. It took me all morning to find where I'd put them.
Paperwork has a way of hiding. All signed?
All signed, in a dark blue pen, which is what I normally use for official paperwork. That way I can always tell the originals from the copies.

gold.rationale: a restatement of the stored contract preference in other words
